answer: Proof-of-Place Commitment. Each identity must publish a signed commitment to a randomly assigned physical location drawn from a public map, such as a karst region or a marble quarry, and periodically prove presence through a local challenge. Duplicates claiming the same location collide and are flagged, since the map has finite slots; the attacker must acquire and maintain distinct real locations, raising per-identity cost to a nadir of sustained logistics rather than a one-time fee.
